title: Maximum residue levels for acetamiprid
summary: EU to increase acetamiprid MRLs for plums, soyabeans, parsley, rosemary, basil and edible flowers from early 2027
update: The European Union (EU) will increase the maximum residue levels (MRLs) for acetamiprid on plums, soyabeans, parsley, rosemary, basil and edible flowers.
impacted_products: Apples, pears, quinces, medlars, apricots, cherries, peaches, plums, table grapes, wine grapes, blackberries, raspberries (red, yellow), blueberries, cranberries, gooseberries (green, red, yellow), currants (black, red, white), elderberries, table olives, bananas, tomatoes, sweet peppers/bell peppers, cucumbers, courgettes, melons, pumpkins, watermelons, broccoli, cauliflowers, head cabbages, lamb’s lettuces/corn salads, Roman rocket/ rucola, lettuces, escaroles/broad-leaved endives, red mustards, spinaches, chards/beet leaves, asparagus, poppy seeds, mustard seeds, gold of pleasure seeds, soyabeans, bovine liver, bovine edible offals (other than liver and kidney), honey, plums, soyabeans, parsley, rosemary, basil and edible flowers
what_changing:
The European Union (EU) will increase the maximum residue level (MRL) for acetamiprid on plums, soyabeans, parsley, rosemary, basil and edible flowers as summarised in Table 1.

This follows previous MRL changes made in January 2025 (Regulation 2025/158 ), June 2025 (Regulation 2025/1212 ), and April 2026 (Regulation (EU) 2026/876 ). These changes are summarised in Table 2.
why: Following an application to modify the existing MRLs for these six food commodities, the European Food Safety Authority concluded the MRLs proposed for plums, soyabeans, parsley, rosemary, basil and edible flowers would not pose a risk for consumers ( EFSA 2025 ).
timeline:
The new MRLs in Table 1 are expected to apply from early 2027 .

The application dates for previous MRL changes are shown in Table 2.
background: MRLs are set in accordance with the rules set out in Regulation 396/2005 . For information on current MRLs for other substances, please consult the EU Pesticide Residues database .
resources: EFSA (2025) Modification of the existing maximum residue level for acetamiprid in various crops and honey . EFSA Journal, 23(12): e9774.
